cover.subtitle: Story Walkthrough Edition
dedication: Step by step, stop by stop, from your first PC to 100%.
cover.footer: Fan-made guide for personal use. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo, Game Freak or The Pokémon Company.

blocks.html: This edition walks you through Pokémon Unbound on New Game+ Expert from your first PC to the Champion, then through the post-game to 100%. Everything is in the order you'll actually play it. Read a stop, play it, tick the boxes, turn the page.

There's a second edition of this guide, the reference edition, with every damage calc and source note laid out by topic. You don't need it to play: every fight plan and every checklist is in here too. Use it when you want to know why a plan works.

1. Clear each stop before you move on. Do the numbered steps in order, grab every item marked Grab now, and finish the boss. Every stop ends with a green Before you move on box. If everything in it is ticked, go to the next stop.
2. You don't have to catch everything. Your Pokédex came over from your old save (the community wikis say so; check it in your test start). So the only catches you need are:

items.html: the Pokémon the steps name for your team (they're always called out in the steps),
anything a mission or an NPC asks for (also called out),
the Gen 8 Pokémon, whose dex entries don't carry over. They need the Gen 8 DexNav setup, so they're in the post-game chapter.

blocks.html: Every area still shows its full Pokémon list with a NOW or LATER tag, in case you want a fresh living dex or just like catching.

3. Don't chase "Later" stuff. Some items and Pokémon need something you don't have yet: Surf, Rock Climb, a better rod. They're tagged LATER with exactly what you need. When you get that thing, a purple Return trip box appears at that point in the guide listing everything it opens up, area by area. So you never have to remember to go back.

4. Read the boss page before you walk in. Every boss has a red The short version box: three or four lines saying who to bring and what to click. Under it is the full plan. Save before every boss. On Expert, losing once is normal: the first try is scouting.
5. Keep your team's levels together. Bosses scale to your highest-level Pokémon. One over-levelled mon makes every boss harder. The level cap stops you going over it anyway.

blocks.title: How a stop is laid out

blocks.html: Each chapter is split into stops: a town, a route or a dungeon, usually with a boss at the end. A stop has the same parts in the same order every time.

items.html: Navy bar: the stop's name and the level cap while you're there.
Gold box (At this stop): what you'll do here, who joins your team, and which bosses are coming.
Walkthrough: numbered steps in the order you play them.
Yellow bars: one per area in the stop. Each has the area's Pokémon (with NOW, LATER or OPTIONAL tags), items split into Grab now and Come back later, and the missions that start there.
Boss pages: a red The short version box, then the boss's team, the team to bring, a prep list, the turn-by-turn plan and an Expect the switch note on when the AI will swap.
Purple box (Return trip): appears the moment you get a new field move or rod, listing everything earlier in the game it opens up.
Green box (Before you move on): the end-of-stop checklist.

blocks.html: Tags you'll see on Pokémon:

cells: You can catch it the moment you're there
Needs that first. It'll be listed again in a Return trip box
Only appears in a random daily swarm. Grab it if you see it

blocks.title: Expert and New Game+ in plain English

blocks.html: Level caps. Your Pokémon can't level past the cap. Beat the boss and the cap goes up.

cells: The Elite Four and the Champion

blocks.html: Bosses are tougher than normal trainers. They scale to your highest level, carry healing items, and from Gym 4 on every trainer has fully trained stats. You can only use four bag items per battle, so you can't potion your way through. And only one Pokémon per battle can Mega Evolve.

What New Game+ gave you. Your six chosen Pokémon came back at Lv 10 in their first form, with their natures, trained stats, abilities, egg moves and held items. Your BP came over, and so did your Pokédex. Money and bag items didn't.
Your carried six for this run:

cells: Fast special attacker for the early gyms, then a Specs nuke all game
Your best early attacker. Super Luck in the lead slot also means wild Pokémon carry rare items more often
Intimidate and doubled prize money. Evolve it with a Fire Stone around Blizzard City
Breeding parent, not a battler. Hand its Scarf to Swinub early
Useful from Rival 2 all the way to the end. Mega from the Barbs fight on

blocks.html: If you haven't set up your old save yet, do the next chapter first. It's the only part of this guide you do before pressing New Game.
You won't use the same six all game. The steps tell you who to catch and when, but here's the shape of it so nothing is a surprise:

cells: Your carried six (minus Ditto) and your starter Beldum. Catch Swinub, Mawile, Azurill and Ducklett on the way
Absol, Heracross, Growlithe, Frogadier, Gabite, Metang, plus Mawile, Azumarill, Kirlia and Shinx for specific fights
Arcanine, Mamoswine, Gardevoir, Metagross, Azumarill and Garchomp come online. Greninja and Absol stay strong
Mega Metagross, Mega Garchomp or Mega Heracross, Mamoswine, Gardevoir, Togekiss, Greninja, Absol, Houndoom
A fixed six (the League chapter explains it)

items.html: Lead with Absol when you're exploring. Super Luck in the first slot makes wild Pokémon far more likely to be holding their rare item.
Keep Growlithe in the party for trainer battles while it holds the Amulet Coin. It doubles your prize money even if it never comes out.
Use the relearner. If your Stat Scanner kept its Notebook upgrade, it works as a portable move relearner. A lot of the team plans rely on it.
Heal before bosses. Several dungeons have a free heal right before the boss (the Chansey in Icicle Cave, the nurse and Chansey on Thundercap Mountain). The steps point them out.
Swap held items between fights. Items move freely between your Pokémon. Each team card says who holds what for that fight.

chapters.title: Before you press New Game: prep your old save

blocks.html: Do everything in this chapter on your old, cleared save. Almost nothing in your bag survives New Game+, so this is where you bank the things that do. Work through it top to bottom and tick as you go. When the last box is ticked, start the real run and turn to the Early game chapter.
Do all of this on the old file. Almost nothing in your bag survives, so the old file is where you bank the things that do.

items.html: Confirm you're on v2.1.1.1 (the Nov 2022 hotfix, still the current build). Held Mega Stones are only reported to carry on this version.
Unlock NG+: become Champion, then beat Aklove at the Ruins of Void in the post-game story. The Hall of Fame alone is not enough.
Back up the cleared save file.
Start a New Game from a copy. The game reads the old save and offers NG+. Choose "Info" on that prompt and read the in-game rules: it is Skeli's own explanation and it outranks every wiki.
In that test start, collect your six from the first PC and check: held items (especially Garchompite), key items, BP total, the Stat Scanner and its upgrade, and which moves each mon arrived with.
Anything missing: go back to the backup, fix it, test again. Only then start the real run.

blocks.html: Your carried mons forget every move except egg moves. A carried mon with no egg moves at all (Ditto in the plan below) is the case I can't predict: I have no source for what moves it arrives with. Check it in the test start. The safe fix is to teach Ralts one egg move first (Destiny Bond or Encore, 15 BP each).

blocks.title: What carries over and what doesn't

cells: Reset to Lv 10 and devolved to base form. They keep nature, ability, IVs, EVs, shininess, egg moves and held item. All other moves are forgotten. Special forms come back as the normal base form.
Yes, except Z-Crystals. Held Mega Stones on v2.1.1.1 (one community wiki; confirm in the test start).
Per both community wikis. Confirm in the Info text.
Only the ones you already own (list below). The Stat Scanner keeps its upgrades.
Yes, except Special Encounter entries (the Gen 8 DexNav ones), which must be caught again.
Yes, including shortcuts like the Crater Town Gym one.
Bottle Caps, Gold Bottle Caps, Ability Capsules, Rare Candies, berries, TMs: all gone.
Gone. Only the party of six comes.

blocks.html: New in NG+

items.html: A stall by the KBT Expressway entrance in Crater Town with the Bottle Cap Lady (IVs, paid in Bottle Caps), the EV Maximizer (BP) and the Nature Changer (BP). Same prices as the Frontier. They stay until you become Champion.
The Egg Move Tutor stands in the Move Relearner's house in Crater Town (BP).
With the Frontier Card carried, the Battle Frontier opens as soon as you reach Seaport City.

Legendaries before the credits: Zeraora is confirmed. Diancie is reported by one source. Heatran looks catchable before the League on any file (its key item comes from a pre-League mission). Cosmog and Volcanion: some pages say NG+ opens them early, but none I could read confirms it, so they're in the post-game chapter.
You can change difficulty at any time (old guide, from the wikis).

blocks.html: Difficulty switching: Beyond Kanto says that on a normal file, if you start on Expert and drop down before becoming Champion, you can't go back up. The wikis say NG+ lets you change difficulty freely. I have not seen those two reconciled. Don't lower the difficulty mid-run until the NG+ Info text confirms you can raise it again.
Each one only carries if you own it.

items.html: Stat Scanner: assistant west of the entrance in Prof. Log's Lab, Frozen Heights. Needs 50 species caught.

Stat Scanner upgrade 1 (Notebook): finish Mission #013 Basic Literacy (read all 40 Trainer Tips signs) and hand the Notebook to the same assistant. The scanner becomes a portable move tutor and move relearner. This is the single most useful thing on the list, see the Training toolkit section.
DexNav: Natasha, 2F of the middle apartment block, Blizzard City. Needs 15 caught.
Dowsing Machine: researcher in the west house, Tehl Town. Needs 30 caught.
Motorcycle: Mission #061 The Black Emboar.
Baby Monitor: Mission #023 Flaming Body (hatch 10 eggs).
Oval Charm: Mission #021 Extreme Hyperosmia.
Catching Charm: Mission #062 The West Borrius Pokédex.
Magma Stone: Mission #039 Master Incubator (hatch 100 eggs). It halves egg cycles and you need it for Heatran (Cinder Volcano), which NG+ opens before the credits.
Porta-PC: Mission #008 And Den There Were None.
Time Turner: Mission #065 The Daily Grind.
Shiny Charm: Ranger in Fallshore City Mission HQ, after 65 completed missions.
ADM: Captain Davy, Seaport City Shipyard, post-game. Bring P500,000 (price conflict, see grey areas). Zeraora (Thundercap Mountain 4F, hidden exit) needs it.
Frontier Card: given the first time you enter the Battle Frontier gate in Seaport City as Champion.

blocks.html: BP is the only grind currency that carries. In NG+ it buys natures, EVs, IVs, abilities, egg moves and held items.

items.html: Bank 10,000+ BP (more if you want Hidden Ability swaps or shinies)
Finish Mission #040 More Than a Game (100 wins across Tower, Mine and Circus; Battle Sands doesn't count; 200 BP)
Finish Mission #029 (beat the Elite Four with 18 monotype teams; 1,000 BP)

cells: EV maximise, one stat (reset to zero is 5 BP per Beyond Kanto)
Ability change, regular / hidden (Battle Circus clown)
4 to 16 in my tutor data (Unbound Wiki); Beyond Kanto says up to 64
Choice Band, Choice Specs, Choice Scarf, Life Orb, Leftovers, Assault Vest, Eviolite, Rocky Helmet, Heavy-Duty Boots
Focus Sash, Weakness Policy, Air Balloon
White Herb, Mental Herb, Power Herb, terrain seeds
Shiny makeover from the Shady Guy (midnight to about 5 AM)

blocks.html: Why 10,000: one fully built new mon costs about 450 BP (Gold Bottle Cap 200, nature 50, two EV maxes 100, held item 48, two or three egg moves 30 to 45). Expert's per-fight teams mean 20 or more mons on top of your carried six. A Hidden Ability swap adds 200 per mon.
Fastest BP farm: not found. I have no solid data on which Frontier facility pays best per hour. Scope Lens is listed at 32 BP in the old guide and 48 BP in my held-item data: check in game.
They come back at Lv 10 with only egg moves, so lock in everything that sticks. Per mon:

items.html: Nature set (Frontier Nature Changer, 50 BP; resets friendship to 0)
IVs maxed (Gold Bottle Cap to the IV lady west of Seaport City Port)
Ability set (Ability Capsule 100 BP, or the Battle Circus clown 100 regular / 200 hidden)
Final EV spread set (EV Maximizer, 50 BP per stat; it can purge too). EVs carry, so set the spread you want at the end of the run, not a training spread.
Egg moves taught (Egg Move Tutor, 15 BP each). These are the only moves that survive.
Held item given (one each; see "What to carry" in the roster section)
In your party at the final save
Optional: shiny makeover (500 BP), cosmetic only

blocks.html: The exact six, with natures, EVs, egg moves and items, are in "Your core roster" below.

items.html: Fill the Pokédex as far as you can. Every entry now is one less to chase later. Special Encounter entries (Regieleki, Regidrago, Enamorus and the other Gen 8 DexNav ones) won't carry. Having any Gen 8 Pokémon registered also carries the Gen 8 flag, which affects DexNav detection and which trainers use Gen 8 mons.
Use every Bottle Cap, Gold Bottle Cap and Ability Capsule on the six.
Spend your money. The ADM is the only purchase that carries.
Don't spend BP on things that won't carry (Rare Candies, spare unheld items). Banked BP is worth more.
Take Z-Crystals off the six and give each a real held item.
Max the Amulet Coin if you can (Tehl Town upgrade NPC, Big Nuggets, show him a Regigigas first). The level is confirmed to carry and it pays for Game Corner items early.
Final save with the six in your party, then back it up again.

blocks.html: Black Trainer Card (max Stat Scanner). The final scanner upgrade edits any of your Pokémon's EVs, IVs, gender, level, nature, ability and Hidden Power from the menu, and evolves from the menu. If that tier survives into NG+, perfecting mons costs nothing and most of the BP budget is spare. Only the first upgrade is confirmed to carry.

items.html: Star 1: become Champion
Star 2: complete every mission (don't release or Cloud-trade the Mission #070 Zygarde)
Star 3: complete the National Pokédex
Star 4: 100-win streak at the Antisis City Ring Challenge
Star 5: all Gold Prints at the Battle Frontier (50-win streak at every facility)
Then take the Stat Scanner to the assistant in Prof. Log's Lab

blocks.html: Unbound Cloud stash. Unbound Cloud (unboundcloud.net) is Skeli's official cloud storage for v2.1.0+ saves: 100 boxes of 30. Your PC boxes don't carry, but mons parked in the Cloud can be pulled into another save. Moving between two saves isn't explicitly documented.

items.html: Stash breeding stock (a perfect Ditto, parents with the right natures and egg moves)
Stash anything from your PC you don't want to lose

blocks.html: Cloud mons keep their level. Traded Pokémon above the cap disobey, and one over-cap mon in your party switches the level cap off for the whole party. Keep them boxed as breeders.

blocks.title: Grey areas to settle in the test start

Put an upgraded Lucky Egg on one of the six, test-start, compare EXP from the first battle.

The changelog confirms the move-editing upgrade carries. Nothing confirms the Black Card tier.
Test-start and open the Stat Scanner.

The Frontier tutors it copies are listed as post-game. Nothing says whether the portable version is gated.
Test-start, open the scanner on a carried mon, try to buy a tutor move.

Held items carry (except Z-Crystals). Unknown if the game lets you give these.
Try "Give". If it works, that's six more perfect-IV builds.

Traded mons above the cap disobey. Unclear if your own old save's mons count as traded.
Withdraw one in the test start and try a battle.
P250,000 (Unbound Wiki) vs P500,000 (Skeli's older FAQ)
4 to 16 BP (Unbound Wiki) vs up to 64 BP (Beyond Kanto)

blocks.html: Only backed by community wikis, not a primary source: BP carrying over, held Mega Stones carrying over, and the Crater Town stall's exact spot. The NG+ Info text settles all three.

chapters.title: Early game: Frozen Heights to Gym 3

blocks.html: Level caps in this chapter: 20 (Gym 1), 26 (Gym 2), 32 (Gym 3). Story order: Rival 1, Rival 2, Gym 1 Mirskle, Marlon at Cinder Volcano, James on the KBT Expressway, Gym 2 Vega, Ivory then Zeph, Rival 3, Gym 3 Alice.

How the builds here were checked. Every move listed is checked against Unbound's own learnset files (the Dynamic Pokémon Expansion source on GitHub, Unbound branch), so "learns at Lv X" is the real Unbound level, not the main-series one. Damage numbers are calc estimates from the Showdown damage calculator using the boss's listed nature and EVs and assuming yours are maxed in the stats shown. Boss rosters are the Expert sets (romhackguides, cross-checked against nuzlockeredux).

Your move relearner is in your pocket. If your carried Stat Scanner has the Notebook upgrade (Mission #013), it works as a portable move relearner and tutor for BP or a Heart Scale. That matters a lot in this chapter: Arcanine gets Burn Up, Flamethrower, Heat Wave and Play Rough straight away, and anything that evolved past a move can get it back. If you don't have the upgrade, #013 (read all 40 Trainer Tips signs) starts in Dresco Town.
Your roster this chapter (full builds are in Front matter, Your core roster):

cells: Metang at 20, the Steel wall for Gyms 1 and 3
Carried six (Gible, Froakie, Absol, Growlithe, Ditto, Heracross)
Lv 10 with your old natures, EVs and egg moves
Mawile: Steel/Fairy with Intimidate. Swinub: your future Mamoswine
Azurill: future Azumarill (catch a Huge Power one). Riolu: Fighting for Vega
Fast Water for Zeph's Mega Houndoom
Kirlia for Vega; a Synchronize one doubles as a nature lead
Magic Guard support (immune to chip and hazards)
Two more Intimidate users for Alice; Abra if you want Synchronize leads

blocks.html: Lead with Absol whenever you're walking around. Super Luck in the lead slot makes wild Pokémon four times as likely to hold their rare item (front matter, Your early toolkit). Swap it out for the boss fights that don't use it.

blocks.title: Frozen Heights, Route 1 and Bellin Town (cap 20)

blocks.html: What you'll do: start the run, pick up your carried six, fight your rival for the first time, and run a quick errand to Bellin Town and back.
Joining your team: Beldum (your starter) and your carried six.
Boss: Rival 1. You're allowed to lose this one.

items.html: Pick Beldum as your starter. You're carrying a Gible, so Beldum gives you something new: it becomes Metang at Lv 20, the Steel wall for Gyms 1 and 3.

Collect your carried six from the first PC as soon as the game lets you. You can only have six in your party, so with Beldum that's one too many: put Ditto back in the PC, but take its Choice Scarf off first. You'll give that to Swinub soon.

Set up held items. Move the Choice Band from Heracross to Absol for now. Growlithe keeps the Amulet Coin (double prize money), Froakie keeps the Choice Specs, Gible keeps the Garchompite. The Life Orb goes in your bag until Marlon.
Talk to Prof. Log and get the Town Map. The assistant west of the lab entrance gives you the Stat Scanner (it needs 50 species caught, which your carried Pokédex may already cover).
Fight Rival 1 when the story calls for it. The plan is on the next page. Win or lose, the story carries on.
Accept Mission #001, then #041 from the old man. Walk through Route 1 to Bellin Town, buy an Antidote at the Mart, and bring it back to him. With Beldum as your starter, you get a Psychic Gem.
Back in Bellin Town, Mission #067 (The Food Thief) starts here: you chase an Alolan Sandslash into Icicle Cave, and that's where you're heading anyway.
Pick up the Zygarde Cells on the way: #001 behind your neighbour's house, #002 on Route 1 southwest of the frozen lake, #003 on the east side of Bellin Town behind the fence.

blocks.html: You're allowed to lose. To win: lead Growlithe (Intimidate), switch to Absol holding the Choice Band, and click Play Rough. If it misses or Gible survives, Growlithe finishes it.

blocks.html: If your carried six are already in the party, you can win it:

items.html: Lead Growlithe. Intimidate drops Gible's Attack. Its Fire Fang is resisted and its Metal Claw only does 15 to 18% to Growlithe after Intimidate.
Turn 1: switch to Absol holding the Choice Band. It takes about 39 to 47% from a -1 Fire Fang on the way in.
Turn 2: Play Rough (Fairy is 2x on Dragon). Calc: 98 to 118% with an Adamant Absol, an 87.5% chance to OHKO. A Jolly Absol only has a 25% chance, so the nature matters here.
Gible is faster, so it gets a second hit in before Play Rough, and Rough Skin chips Absol when Play Rough makes contact. If Gible survives or you miss, Absol is out of HP: finish with Growlithe.
Backup: if you put the Band on Growlithe instead, it can win alone with Close Combat (43 to 53% each), but Sand Attack makes that a coin flip.

blocks.html: Expect the switch: he only has Gible, so there's nothing to switch to.
Grab now:

Cell #001 (Zygarde Cell): Frozen Heights, behind the neighbour's house

blocks.html: What you'll do: cross Icicle Cave, beat Rival 2 on 2F, and come out onto Route 2. This is the first big catching stop: four of the Pokémon you grab here end up on your team.
Joining your team: Swinub, Mawile, Azurill. Also catch an Alolan Sandshrew (to trade), Scraggy and Riolu.
Boss: Rival 2 on 2F. Heal at the Chansey on 3F afterwards.

items.html: Get Froakie to Lv 16 before Rival 2 so it evolves into Frogadier. The Rival 2 plan leads with it.
Catch a Swinub in the cave. This is your future Mamoswine, one of the best Pokémon in the run. Give it Ditto's Choice Scarf.
Detour into the Tablet Cavern for Mawile. You want one with Intimidate (it can also be Hyper Cutter or Sheer Force). Keep catching until you get one.
Detour into the Sandslash Lair for an Alolan Sandshrew. It's a trade for Ducklett in Dresco Town, the next stop. This is also where Mission #067's food thief runs to.
Beat Rival 2 on 2F. Plan on the next page. He gives you the Safety Goggles: put them on Heracross straight away, they're its item for Gym 1.
Heal at the Chansey on 3F.

Out on Route 2, catch Azurill, Scraggy and Riolu. Azurill needs Huge Power (one of its two normal abilities): keep catching until you get it. It becomes Azumarill, which hits harder than almost anything you'll have for a while.
Work through the area pages below for items (TMs, Zygarde Cells) before you leave.

blocks.html: Mawile's ability matters. Mawile can be Hyper Cutter, Intimidate or (Hidden) Sheer Force in Unbound. You want Intimidate: it's half the reason Mawile is good for Alice. Catch until you get one, or DexNav for it.

Lead Frogadier: Water Pulse kills his Swinub. Switch to Absol for his Gible: Play Rough kills it. Sand Veil makes it dodge sometimes, so if it misses, click it again. Backups: Heracross or Growlithe for Swinub, Growlithe for Gible.

blocks.html: Turn by turn

items.html: Lead Gible + Heracross against her Floette + Gloom.
Turn 1: Gible uses Sandstorm. The fog is gone and the sand chips all four of hers every turn; Gible ignores it and the Goggles protect Heracross. Heracross uses Rock Blast on Floette.
Turn 2: Gible's Iron Head and Heracross's Rock Blast both into Floette. Together that's well over 100%, so Wish can't save it.
Then Gloom: Aerial Ace plus Iron Head. Its Sleep Powder can only hit Gible; keep the Awakening for that.
Kill order after that: Comfey, then Weedle. Always put both attacks into the same mon. Comfey: Iron Head plus Rock Blast (or Metang's Metal Claw). Weedle: Aerial Ace kills it.
Gible is the one taking hits (Fairy Wind does about half). When it drops under half, switch it to Growlithe, which resists Fairy, Grass and Bug.
If the sandstorm runs out (five turns) and the fog matters, bring Gible back to reset it, or Ducklett to Defog.

blocks.html: Expect the switch: double battle, so she won't swap a mon out just because you can KO it. In doubles the AI only switches to bring in a mon that absorbs your attack (Flash Fire, Sap Sipper and the like) or to pull a mon with nothing useful to click. None of hers has an absorbing ability, and they all carry Wish, Ingrain or healing support, so expect them to stay in. That's why focusing one target at a time works.
Watch out

items.html: Grass Knot is neutral on Gible (Grass is 2x on Ground but Dragon resists it), and Floette's Fairy Wind is its real threat at about half its HP.
Rock Blast hits two to five times and each hit can miss in the fog, so the sandstorm on turn 1 matters.

Backup plan: lead Gible + Growlithe. Turn 1 Sandstorm plus Flame Wheel on Gloom, then the same kill order, doubling every turn: Iron Head plus Flame Wheel, or Iron Head plus Metang's Metal Claw. If Gloom puts Growlithe to sleep, switch to Metang. Ducklett clears the fog if Gible goes down.

lead_fields: It's a multi battle, so the game only lets you take three. The first three are the plan; the last three are swaps if one of them isn't ready.

blocks.html: Prep: bag 2 Super Potions, 1 Burn Heal, 1 Revive. Heal at the Chansey right before.
Turn by turn

items.html: Lead Absol. Expect two Fake Outs on turn 1 (Sableye and Shiftry both carry it). Will-O-Wisp from Sableye fails on a Dark type.

Kill Shiftry and Swoobat first. Shiftry: Megahorn (4x). Swoobat: Knock Off. Both are faster than Absol and hit it for about half (Air Cutter 48 to 58%, Leaf Tornado 52 to 62%), so Absol takes one hit and kills. After two kills, Life Orb recoil has it low: switch out.

Growlithe comes in on Cacnea (it resists Needle Arm and Fell Stinger, and Fire Fang OHKOs it). Mawile comes in on Shiftry or Swoobat, which can't hurt it much. Keep Mawile away from Sableye: Will-O-Wisp does work on it.

Sableye: Absol's Play Rough (OHKO). Duskull: Absol's Knock Off (OHKO through Eviolite). Hit Duskull from full so it never gets to Destiny Bond you; if it's already low and has moved before you, let Jax take it.
Pickpocket: Shiftry steals your item if you make contact and it survives. Megahorn OHKOs it, so that only matters if you hit it with something weaker.

blocks.html: Expect the switch: a multi battle counts as a double battle, so no dodge-a-KO switching. The only absorber on their side is Cacnea (Water Absorb), and none of your three or Jax's mons uses a Water move, so it never comes into play.

blocks.html: What you'll do: walk Routes 4 and 5 into Crater Town, home of Gym 2. Crater Town is where you start properly building your team: the NG+ stall, the Egg Move Tutor and the Move Relearner are all here.
Joining your team: Ralts (Route 4), Clefairy (Crater Town). Note Houndour on Route 5 at night for later.
Bosses: none in town, but James on the KBT Expressway comes before the Gym.

items.html: On Route 4, catch a Ralts. It becomes Kirlia at Lv 20, your Choice Specs Fairy attacker for Vega. A Synchronize one doubles as a nature lead later.
On Route 5, look for Houndour at night. You don't need it yet, but it becomes Houndoom, which joins for the late game.
In Crater Town, find the NG+ stall by the KBT entrance. It changes natures and maxes EVs for BP. Run every new team member through it before its first boss.

Visit the Move Relearner's house. The Egg Move Tutor there teaches moves for 15 BP each: Icicle Crash for Swinub, Aqua Jet and Belly Drum for Azumarill. The Move Relearner in the same house restores Lv 1 moves for a Heart Scale.
Get a Clefairy from the Pokémon Center, behind the bookcases. You want one with Magic Guard: Vega's gym chips your HP every turn and Magic Guard ignores it.
Don't go into the Gym yet. Head onto the KBT Expressway next: James comes first.

blocks.html: What you'll do: fight through four Team Granbull goons and their boss James. Beating him gets you the Motorcycle.
Boss: James, a single battle with a Poison-heavy team.

Lead Metang: Steel is immune to Poison, so his main attacks and Toxic Spikes do nothing to it. Kill Accelgor first with Growlithe's Fire Fang before Toxic Spikes pile up. Then Gabite's Bulldoze for Alolan Grimer, Azumarill's Banded Aqua Jet for Pignite, and Metang walls Koffing.
A singles fight after four goons. Reward: TM98 Work Up and the Motorcycle (Mission #061).

items.html: Lead Metang. Acid Spray can't touch it (Steel is immune to Poison), Struggle Bug is only neutral, and Toxic Spikes can't poison a Steel type. Metal Claw it while you wait for Growlithe's turn, or switch straight to Growlithe and Fire Fang (2x).
Kill Accelgor early. Every layer of Toxic Spikes poisons your grounded switch-ins; Metang and Mawile are immune.
Alolan Grimer: Gabite's Bulldoze (2x). Bulldoze isn't contact, so Poison Touch can't trigger. Kill it before Minimize stacks.

Pignite: Azumarill's Banded Aqua Jet (89 to 107%). Azumarill takes only 16 to 20% from Low Sweep, so it can afford a second Aqua Jet. Backup: Gabite's Bulldoze (58 to 68%, 2HKO). Don't count on Metang here: Confusion is 2x but it's Metang's weak side and only does 23 to 28%.
Koffing: Metang walls it completely. Gabite's Bulldoze can't hit it (Levitate), so use Metal Claw or Confusion.

blocks.html: Expect the switch: the one KO he could dodge is Banded Aqua Jet on Pignite (priority means Azumarill moves first). But nothing he has walls Azumarill: Grimer and Koffing are the bulkiest and still take 43 to 53% from Aqua Jet, which is too much for the AI to call a safe switch. So expect Pignite to stay in. Koffing's Levitate makes Bulldoze miss, but the AI doesn't switch in for a plain immunity unless your hit would KO, and Bulldoze doesn't KO Grimer.

blocks.html: Absol is your anchor: it's immune to the gym's chip damage and its Play Rough is 2x on all four of hers. Lead Growlithe for Intimidate: Close Combat kills Weavile and Liepard. Absol's Play Rough handles her Absol (two hits) and Honchkrow. Switch into Absol, Clefairy or Swinub whenever you need a free turn.

meta: Negative emotions: your active mon loses 1/12 of its HP every turn on Expert. Dark and Ghost types, and Oblivious, Unaware and Magic Guard, are immune.

blocks.html: No Mega on Expert (Mega Absol is Insane only).
Why it's hard: the chip damage eats your HP every turn, Fake Out and Swagger waste your turns, Super Luck crits ignore your Intimidate, and Liepard's Play Rough OHKOs Scraggy (135 to 163%).
Your Absol is the answer. It's Dark, so the chip doesn't touch it, Psycho Cut can't hit it and Knock Off and Punishment are resisted. Its carried Play Rough is 2x on all four of hers.

Fairy Wind isn't a real answer here. Mawile only has Fairy Wind at this level, and it's a weak 40-power special move (Mawile's Sp. Atk is poor). Mawile doesn't get Play Rough until Lv 48. Your Fairy damage comes from Absol's Play Rough, Kirlia's Choice Specs Draining Kiss and Clefairy's Disarming Voice; Growlithe's Close Combat is the other big hitter.

blocks.html: Prep checklist

items.html: Run Kirlia, Clefairy and Swinub through the Crater Town stall, and buy Swinub's Icicle Crash from the Egg Move Tutor
Bag: 2 Super Potions, 1 Persim Berry (cures Swagger confusion) or Full Heal, 1 Revive
Hold nothing valuable on anything that will take a hit from Liepard: Thief steals it for the fight

blocks.html: Turn by turn

items.html: Lead Growlithe. Intimidate goes up on her lead whatever happens. Expect Fake Out (Liepard or Weavile).
Weavile: Close Combat (100 to 120%, OHKO), or switch to Heracross and Banded Revenge (OHKO). Its Dark Gem Punishment does 72 to 88% to Growlithe but only 21 to 26% to Heracross.

Liepard: Close Combat OHKOs it (117 to 140%). If Liepard has already eaten its Lum Berry, Unburden has doubled its Speed and it moves first: switch to Clefairy (Magic Guard ignores the chip, Charm blunts it and Disarming Voice 2HKOs it), or take the Play Rough on Growlithe (Fire resists Fairy) and Close Combat back.

Her Absol (bulky): your Absol's Play Rough twice (77 to 94% each). Her Knock Off only does 25 to 30% to your Absol and Psycho Cut can't hit it, so this is a safe trade. Kirlia's Draining Kiss (68 to 82%) works too, but her Knock Off can OHKO Kirlia (86 to 102%).
Honchkrow: Absol's Play Rough (OHKO), Kirlia's Specs Draining Kiss (88 to 102%) or Swinub's Icicle Crash (77 to 94%). Swagger confuses you but raises your Attack, so attack through it.

Liepard and your Absol: Liepard is faster and its Play Rough does 83 to 99% to Absol (57 to 68% after Intimidate). Bring Absol in on Liepard only after Intimidate has gone up, then Play Rough OHKOs it.
The chip: every turn a non-immune mon sits in, it loses 1/12. Switch into Absol, Clefairy or Swinub whenever you need a free turn.

blocks.html: Expect the switch: hardly any. Liepard, Weavile and her Absol are all faster than whatever OHKOs them, and a faster mon never switches to dodge. Heracross's Revenge always moves last (-4 priority), so it never triggers a dodge either. Honchkrow is a touch slower than your Absol, but nothing on her team resists Fairy or walls Absol, so it has nowhere to go.
Watch out

items.html: Scraggy is out of this team because Liepard's Play Rough OHKOs it. Absol does its job (chip-immune, resists Dark) and hits far harder.
Super Luck crits ignore Intimidate and stat drops. Don't rely on Intimidate alone against Honchkrow.
Keep Heracross away from Honchkrow (Air Cutter is 4x and OHKOs it) and from her Absol's Psycho Cut if it's low (54 to 66%).
Backup plan: if Growlithe goes down early, Heracross carries the Fighting damage, and Clefairy's Charm plus Life Dew buys turns against the physical attackers.

blocks.html: What you'll do: leave Crater Town south and get ambushed: Ivory, then Zeph's Mega Houndoom, back to back with no healing and no team change in between. Then on through Valley Cave.
Your six for both fights: Absol, Heracross, Growlithe, Azumarill, Frogadier, Gabite. Use Absol and Heracross on Ivory and keep the other four fresh for Zeph.
Bosses: Ivory, then Zeph.

items.html: Get all six to Lv 32 before you leave Crater Town. Route 5 and the KBT Expressway are good for grinding. Buizel should be Floatzel (Lv 26) by now too, even though it sits this one out.
Give the Choice Band to Azumarill. You can't swap items between the two fights, and the Band on Azumarill is the safer plan for Zeph. Heracross still 2HKOs Ivory's team without it.
Heal, save, and walk out of Crater Town to the south. The fights start straight away.
Beat Ivory with Absol and Heracross (plan below).
Beat Zeph's Mega Houndoom with Growlithe's Intimidate and Azumarill's Banded Aqua Jet (plan below).
Go back for HM01 Cut. The mountain climber on the KBT Expressway, south of Crater Town, gives it to you after the Zeph fight. A Return trip box below lists what it opens up.
Head into Valley Cave and work through its area page.

blocks.html: These trigger the moment you leave Crater Town south. They're back to back with no healing and no team change between them, so you pick one six for both. Use three mons on Ivory and keep three fresh for Zeph's Mega Houndoom.
Get to the cap first. Floatzel (Buizel evolves at 26), Gabite and Azumarill should all be at 32 before you walk out of Crater Town. Grind on Route 5 and the KBT Expressway.

blocks.html: One Choice Band, two users. You can't change held items between the two fights, so decide before you leave Crater Town. The Band on Azumarill is the safer Zeph plan; Heracross still 2HKOs everything on Ivory's side without it. Calcs above for Heracross assume the Band, so expect about two-thirds of that damage if Azumarill has it.
Azumarill doesn't have Aqua Tail yet. It learns Aqua Tail at Lv 40 in Unbound, so at cap 32 its only physical Water move is Aqua Jet. That's why it holds the Choice Band here.
Ivory: lead Absol. Knock Off kills Kadabra and Misdreavus, and Play Rough or Heracross's Rock Blast takes two hits on Eviolite Vullaby. Swap to Heracross when Absol's Life Orb has it under a third.
Zeph: switch Growlithe in first for Intimidate, then Azumarill's Banded Aqua Jet (it moves first). Frogadier's Water Pulse or a second Aqua Jet finishes. Gabite is the safety net.
Vs Ivory (use Absol and Heracross; keep Growlithe, Azumarill, Frogadier and Gabite fresh)

items.html: Lead Absol. Kadabra's Psybeam can't touch it, Misdreavus's Hex is resisted (18 to 23%) and Absol is faster than Misdreavus.

Misdreavus: Knock Off (85 to 104%). It will Will-O-Wisp Absol back, which halves Absol's damage, but a burned Knock Off still finishes it. If you'd rather not take the burn, switch to Heracross instead: the burn only turns on Guts, and Night Slash 2HKOs it.
Kadabra: Absol's Knock Off (OHKO). Kadabra's Psybeam does 64 to 78% to Heracross, so Kadabra is Absol's job.

Vullaby has Eviolite, so it takes two hits from anything: Absol's Play Rough (63 to 76%) or Heracross's Rock Blast (63 to 75%, 2x). Its Rock Tomb only does 24 to 28% to Absol. Flatter confuses you but raises your Sp. Atk; just keep attacking.
Watch Absol's HP. Life Orb costs 10% per hit. Once it's under a third, finish with Heracross.

blocks.html: Expect the switch (Ivory): Kadabra is faster than Absol, so it never dodges. Misdreavus is slower, but Knock Off only has a small chance to OHKO it, and Ivory has no wall to bring in anyway: Vullaby resists Dark but Play Rough still 2HKOs it through Eviolite. If Vullaby does come in on a Knock Off, that's a good trade: Knock Off strips its Eviolite, and after that Play Rough does 92 to 111%.
Vs Zeph's Mega Houndoom (one mon, Adamant, max Attack)

items.html: Switch Growlithe in first to drop Houndoom's Attack with Intimidate. Its Fire Fang is resisted.
Then Azumarill. Banded Aqua Jet: 84 to 102%. It moves first thanks to priority, so Houndoom's Sucker Punch (resisted) is its only answer.

If Aqua Jet doesn't kill, Frogadier's Specs Water Pulse (76 to 90%) or a second Aqua Jet finishes it. Frogadier takes 58 to 70% from a -1 Thunder Fang, so bring it in after the Intimidate, not before.
If Houndoom uses Howl, it's +1. Don't give it a second Howl: attack immediately.
Gabite is the safety net. Fire Fang does only 25 to 29% to it and Thunder Fang can't touch it. Bulldoze (53 to 65%) twice wins.

blocks.html: Turn by turn

items.html: Lead Metang against Minior. It resists Ancient Power and Acrobatics (16 to 19%). Metal Claw twice (76 to 90% each). Minior will set Stealth Rock on turn 1: accept it. Every switch-in now takes Rock chip, and Gyarados loses a quarter of its HP each time (Rock is 2x on it), so plan your switches. If Shields Down drops (below half HP), Minior's core form is faster and frailer: Bullet Punch finishes it. Faster option: after any KO, send Frogadier in and Specs Water Pulse OHKOs Minior outright.

Rotate Intimidate. Every switch-in from Arcanine, Mawile, Gyarados or Luxio cuts her physical attackers again. Gliscor's Hyper Cutter blocks it (and so does Mega Pinsir's before it Mega Evolves), so don't waste switches on those.

Gliscor: Gyarados's Ice Fang (59 to 69%, 2HKO). Gyarados is immune to Bulldoze and resists Fire Fang. Frogadier's Specs Water Pulse (83 to 98%) finishes it, but Gem Acrobatics does 91 to 108% to Frogadier, so only bring it in once Gliscor is already hurt.

Mega Pinsir: switch Metang or Mawile into it (they take 15 to 23% from Double Hit), then bring Arcanine in and Burn Up (94 to 113%, 75% chance to OHKO). If Burn Up leaves it alive, Extreme Speed finishes it. Burn Up removes Arcanine's Fire type for the rest of the fight, which only matters against Gliscor's Fire Fang.
Crobat is the only special attacker. Metang walls it (Venoshock can't touch Steel; Air Cutter 8 to 11%). Luxio's Spark (2x) or Metang's chip damage finishes it.
Dodrio: Mawile takes 25 to 30% from Steel Wing. Let it soak, then finish with Luxio's Spark or Arcanine's Extreme Speed (priority; 42 to 50%) plus anything.

blocks.html: Expect the switch: hardly any dodging. The permanent Tailwind doubles the Speed of every mon she has, so they're all faster than yours, and a faster mon never switches to dodge a KO. None of hers has an absorbing ability either.

The switch you can cause is the Intimidate one. A physical attacker at -3 Attack switches out, and that resets the drops. Three Intimidates on Dodrio or Minior will do it (Gliscor's Hyper Cutter and pre-Mega Pinsir's block it). So once one of them is at -2, attack instead of bringing in a fourth Intimidate.
Watch out

items.html: Knock Off (Gliscor and Dodrio) removes Metang's Eviolite. If Eviolite gets knocked off, Metang is still a Steel type but no longer near-unkillable: bring Mawile in for the walling instead.
Old guide correction: Mawile's Sucker Punch does only 15 to 18% to Mega Pinsir (it has 252 Defence on Expert). Mega Pinsir is Arcanine's job.
Backup plan: if Arcanine goes down before Mega Pinsir, Metang and Mawile can still wall it while Luxio and Gyarados chip; Rock Tomb lowers Speed and Brick Break is neutral on both.

items.html: Ariados: Arcanine's Flamethrower (78 to 95%), then Extreme Speed finishes through the Sash. Its Smart Strike does under 10% to Arcanine. If it Swords Dances, it still can't break Arcanine before you kill it.

Granbull: keep Arcanine in. Intimidate cuts its Attack, Fire resists Spirit Break (15 to 17% at -1) and Thunder Fang does about the same. Flamethrower three times wins, or swap to Metang for Metal Claw. Never let Greninja, Heracross, Absol or Gabite take a Fairy Gem Spirit Break.

Probopass: Heracross's Arm Thrust. Fighting is 4x and every hit after the first goes through Sturdy, so two hits kill (90%). Its Power Gem does only 25 to 30% to Heracross. Backup: Gabite's Bulldoze (4x, two hits for Sturdy) or Greninja's Water Pulse.
Crawdaunt: Heracross's Brick Break (OHKO). Hyper Cutter stops Intimidate, but its Aqua Jet only does 22 to 27% to Heracross.

blocks.html: The roster is the Difficult-mode team (no Expert data anywhere), and no natures or EVs are listed, so the calcs assume none. Expect a little less damage if Expert gives them EVs.

Expect the switch: Heracross is faster than Crawdaunt and Probopass, so both could look for a dodge. Ariados and Granbull resist Fighting, but neither walls Heracross: Rock Blast is 2x on Ariados, and Granbull's Defence is far below Heracross's Attack. So the AI has nothing to bring in, and they stay in. None of his mons absorbs Fire or Water either.

Why it's hard: it's two trainers at once under Psychic Terrain (no priority moves against your grounded mons), with Meowstic's Prankster Reflect, Oranguru's Instruct making Alakazam fire twice, Mismagius's Magic Bounce and Destiny Bond, and an Incineroar that hits hard.

Your Absol wrecks it. Four of the five are Psychic or Ghost, Absol is immune to every Psychic move they have, and Life Orb Knock Off OHKOs all four. Your job is to keep it away from Alakazam's Dazzling Gleam and Incineroar's Drain Punch.

items.html: Lead Absol + Arcanine. Intimidate hits Incineroar. Arcanine resists Fairy and Fire, so it's the safe partner.

Turn 1: Absol Knock Offs Alakazam if it's out (OHKO). Alakazam is faster and its Dazzling Gleam does 76 to 89% to Absol, so if you'd rather not risk it, Protect Absol on turn 1 and Crunch Alakazam with Arcanine, then Knock Off whatever's left next turn.

Then Knock Off everything Psychic or Ghost: Meowstic, Oranguru, Mismagius. Each one dies to one hit. Kill Mismagius from full: Destiny Bond only matters when it's low. Life Orb costs Absol 10% per hit, so after three kills, rest it.

Incineroar is the one that kills Absol (Drain Punch does 101 to 120%). Never leave Absol in when Incineroar can target it. Greninja's Water Pulse (2x, 66 to 77%) or Floatzel's Flip Turn handle it once Intimidate is down.
Screens: Meowstic's Reflect halves your physical damage. Absol's Knock Off still OHKOs the frail ones through it most of the time; if it doesn't, Scraggy's Brick Break removes it.

blocks.html: Expect the switch: double battle, so no dodge-a-KO switching, and nobody on their side has an absorbing ability. The switch to watch is Intimidate: you have three users (Arcanine, Scraggy, Gyarados), and a physical attacker at -3 Attack switches out, which resets its drops. If Incineroar is at -2, kill it instead of bringing in the third Intimidate. Mismagius's Magic Bounce sends status moves back at you, so don't aim Will-O-Wisp or Thunder Wave at it.

blocks.html: How Inverse works: super-effective hits become resisted, resisted hits become super effective, and immunities become super effective. For this gym that means:

items.html: Ghost moves are 2x on all of her Normal types (the immunity flips). That's every mon she has.
Fighting moves are resisted by Normal types. Don't use them.
Her Fighting moves hit Fairy, Psychic, Flying, Poison, Bug and Ghost types 2x; Gardevoir and Togekiss take 4x. Leave them home.
Dark types resist Fighting in inverse (Dark is normally weak to it).
Electric is 2x on Heliolisk (Electric normally resists Electric).

blocks.html: Two traps from the old guide: Ancient Power is a special move, and Piloswine's Sp. Atk is so low it does about 5% even before the type chart; don't plan around it. And Mawile takes 2x or more from Round, Psybeam and Signal Beam in inverse: leave it home.

No Shadow Ball yet. Ghost moves are the only thing that's 2x on her pure Normal types, but TM30 Shadow Ball is on a Route 9 island you need Surf for, and Surf only comes from your rival on Route 12, after this gym. Greninja's Shadow Sneak (relearn it: a Greninja Lv 18 move) is your only Ghost move here, and it's weak (31 to 40% on Porygon-Z). So this fight is won with Intimidate and raw damage, not type tricks.

Two things the inverse chart does give you: Bewear and Mega Lopunny are Normal/Fighting, so Dark and Bug moves are 2x on them here (Fighting normally resists those). And Dark types resist her Fighting moves. That makes Absol your Lopunny killer.

blocks.html: Prep: bag 2 Hyper Potions, 1 Paralyze Heal (Thunder Wave), 1 Revive.
Turn by turn

items.html: Lead Arcanine and expect Fake Out. Intimidate goes up.
Don't Will-O-Wisp Bewear or Lopunny. A burned Facade doubles in power and ignores the burn. Burn Miltank (Body Slam, no Facade).
Rotate Intimidate. Four of your six have it. Every switch cuts Bewear, Miltank and Lopunny's Attack again, faster than Power-Up Punch can rebuild it.

Mega Lopunny outspeeds everything you have. Get one Intimidate on it, then bring Absol in on a Fighting move (resisted here) and Night Slash: it's 2x in inverse and OHKOs. At -1, its Facade only does 38 to 45% to Absol.

Bewear: Fluffy halves contact damage, but Absol's Megahorn still 2HKOs it (60 to 71%). Careful: its Payback is 2x on Absol here (64 to 76% even at -1), so only stay in if you're healthy. Greninja's Water Pulse isn't contact (49 to 59%).
Porygon-Z is special, so Intimidate does nothing. Greninja's Specs Water Pulse 2HKOs it before Recover adds up. Its Psybeam is 2x on Absol here (68 to 82%), so keep Absol out.
Miltank: burn it with Arcanine, then Greninja's Water Pulse or Absol's Night Slash. Its Ice Punch does 44 to 53% to Greninja, so don't trade hits forever.
Heliolisk: Luxray's Spark (2x here). Gyarados takes a quarter from Parabolic Charge.

blocks.html: Community alternative: RetroAchievements players beat Expert Mel with Sticky Web, Toxic Spikes and Hex Gengar. Gastly is in Grim Woods and gets Hex at Lv 24 as Haunter, but a Ghost type takes 2x from her Normal moves and 4x from Fighting here, so it needs that hazard support to work.

Expect the switch: no dodging to worry about: Mega Lopunny and Heliolisk are faster than what hits them hard, and nothing else here gets OHKO'd. None of hers absorbs anything. The Intimidate cycle is the catch. A physical attacker at -3 Attack switches out, and that resets its drops to zero. With four Intimidate users it's easy to overshoot, so stop at -2: once Bewear, Miltank or Lopunny is at -2, attack it instead of switching in another Intimidate. If it does switch out at -3, the mon that comes in eats the next Intimidate, so you lose nothing but tempo.

items.html: Lead Metagross. Toucannon's Pluck, Fury Attack and Rock Blast are all resisted.

His Mamoswine sets Stealth Rock early. Switch to Heracross and Brick Break (OHKO; Heracross is faster). Its Ice Fang does 51 to 61% to Heracross if you take a hit on the way in. Backup: Metagross's Hammer Arm (81 to 96%) or Azumarill's Aqua Tail. Thick Fat halves Fire and Ice, so your Mamoswine is the wrong answer.

Fraxure: kill it before Dragon Dance stacks: Azumarill's Play Rough or Absol's Play Rough (both OHKO). Fraxure is faster than Absol: its Dual Chop does 71 to 85% unboosted, but a +1 Dual Chop OHKOs Absol, so bring Absol in before it has danced. Mold Breaker ignores abilities like Thick Fat and Levitate on your side.
Vaporeon: Luxray's Wild Charge (64 to 77%). Never use Water moves on it.
Gabite: your Scarf Mamoswine's Icicle Crash (OHKO), or Absol's Play Rough (OHKO; it survives Gabite's Dragon Claw at 60 to 72%).
Stealth Rock will be up all fight. Count it in: every switch-in loses 1/8 (Heracross 1/8, Absol 1/8).

blocks.html: Expect the switch: he can try to dodge two of your KOs (Brick Break on his Mamoswine, Scarf Icicle Crash on Gabite), but nothing on his team walls you: Toucannon resists Fighting and eats a 2x Rock Blast, and Vaporeon and his Mamoswine resist Ice but can't take Mamoswine's Bulldoze and raw Attack. Vaporeon is the real switch risk. Water Absorb means any Water move you aim at another mon can pull Vaporeon in for free healing, so keep Azumarill's Aqua Tail and Aqua Jet unclicked until Vaporeon is gone. Play Rough is the safe button.

Bring: Absol (Dark: immune to the chip, resists Dark, and its Play Rough is 2x on every Dark type), Scrafty (same chip immunity, plus Intimidate), Azumarill (Play Rough is 2x on Dark types and Fairy resists Dark), Mamoswine (Oblivious makes it chip-immune per Unbound Wiki; Ice is 2x on Honchkrow), Gardevoir (Dazzling Gleam hits both foes 2x). Expect the switch: a two-on-one double, so no dodge-a-KO switching. I don't know his Expert team, so I can't tell you about absorbers; check his first sends before you click any Fire, Water, Electric or Grass move.

blocks.html: Prep: bag 2 Hyper Potions, 2 Full Heals (Toxic).

items.html: Lead Metagross: immune to Toxic and Venoshock, so the two poisoners can't touch it.

Mightyena and Exploud: Heracross's Brick Break OHKOs both, and Heracross is faster. Mightyena's Psychic Fangs would OHKO Heracross back, so only bring Heracross in at full HP. Exploud's Flamethrower does 56 to 67% to it.

Umbreon: Heracross's Brick Break twice (68 to 81% each). Foul Play is resisted (35 to 41%), and if Umbreon Toxics Heracross, Guts makes it hit harder. Gardevoir works too: Foul Play uses Gardevoir's low Attack, so Calm Mind once and Dazzling Gleam.

Decidueye: Absol's Knock Off (OHKO; Absol is just faster). Spirit Shackle stops you switching out, so make sure Absol is the one in front of it. Low Sweep does 79 to 93% to Absol. Backup: Arcanine's Flamethrower (2x).
Azumarill is the spare: Play Rough on Mightyena or Umbreon.

blocks.html: Expect the switch: Gengar is the one to watch. It's immune to Fighting, and the AI will switch an immune mon in if it outspeeds your attacker, even when your other moves hurt it. So when Heracross goes for Brick Break on Mightyena or Exploud, or Arcanine goes for Close Combat on Exploud, Gengar can come in. That's why Gengar goes first in this plan: once Metagross has killed it, your Fighting moves have nothing to dodge into. Decidueye is also immune to Fighting, but it's slower and Night Slash or Flamethrower 2HKOs it, so it won't come in for that.

Turn 1: Arcanine Close Combat on Alolan Golem (58 to 69%) or Will-O-Wisp it to halve its Galvanize Return. Mamoswine attacks Golem too (Icicle Crash is neutral) to kill it fast; it's his biggest damage dealer. If Golem is still standing, Heracross's Brick Break nearly OHKOs it on its own (90 to 107%).
Trick Room lasts five turns. Spend them on Bronzong's partner, not Bronzong, or Protect and switch to stall them out.
Escavalier: Arcanine's Burn Up (OHKO). Burn Up removes Arcanine's Fire type afterwards, so Golem's Rock Slide is no longer super effective on it.

Lanturn: Heracross's Brick Break (68 to 80%) plus Gardevoir's Specs Magical Leaf (37 to 45%) on the same turn kills it. Its Scald can burn your physical attackers; a burn only switches on Heracross's Guts.
Ampharos: no easy weakness while it floats. Heracross's Brick Break (57 to 68%) plus a Mega Metagross Iron Head, or Bulldoze under Gravity. Its Thunderbolt does 54 to 64% to Heracross.
With Clefable's Gravity up, Mamoswine's Bulldoze hits everything for five turns. That's the RetroAchievements plan.

blocks.html: Expect the switch: Primarina is the switch-in that will catch you out. It resists Water and Ice, and nothing Greninja has even 3HKOs it (Specs Ice Beam and Surf do only 21 to 26%), so the AI rates it a perfect wall. When Greninja goes for Ice Beam on Roserade or Togekiss (both slower than Greninja), expect Primarina to come in instead. Greninja is then Specs-locked into Ice Beam, and Primarina's Moonblast kills it.

items.html: Fix: kill Primarina first, with Luxray's Wild Charge (OHKO), before Greninja ever clicks Ice Beam.
If it happens anyway: switch Greninja straight to Luxray. Primarina can't switch again for a turn, so Wild Charge lands.
After any Greninja KO the same thing applies: his replacement is picked to beat your active mon, and against Greninja that's Primarina.
Mega Metagross's Iron Head is safe: Klefki and Primarina resist Steel, but Brick Break and Hammer Arm hit them too hard for the AI to call them walls. None of hers absorbs anything.

blocks.html: What you'll do: three fights in and around Antisis City: a Science Society scientist with three exploding Electrode, Team Ferrothorn's boss Barbs (who gives you Heracronite), and Gym 6.
Boss: Big Mo. In his gym, heavier Pokémon move first.

items.html: Heads up: healing costs P500 at the Antisis Pokémon Center.
The three Electrode: use non-contact attacks only (Aftermath hurts whoever lands the KO with contact). Mamoswine's Bulldoze or Earthquake, or Greninja's Specs Surf.
Barbs at Ferrothorn Turf: you can't run from this one. Plan below. He gives you the Heracronite: Heracross can Mega Evolve from now on.
Gym 6: Big Mo. Read the plan: the weight rule flips who moves first.

blocks.text: Science Society Scientist: three Electrode with Explosion

blocks.html: Non-contact attacks only. Mamoswine's Bulldoze or Earthquake (2x), or Greninja's Specs Surf. Metagross resists Explosion. Leave Absol and Heracross out: their attacks are contact moves.

Lv 53, Normal Gem, Aftermath. Metagross resists Explosion. Use non-contact attacks, because Aftermath hurts whoever makes contact for the KO: Mamoswine's Earthquake or Bulldoze (2x) is ideal, and Greninja's Specs Surf (82 to 97%) works too. Don't use Absol or Heracross here: their attacks are contact moves.

blocks.text: Black Ferrothorn Boss Barbs (Ferrothorn Turf). Difficult data.

blocks.html: Arcanine's Flamethrower is 4x on Ferrothorn and 2x on Mega Heracross (and it's special, so Iron Barbs doesn't hurt you). Mamoswine's Earthquake for Alolan Muk before Minimize stacks, Icicle Crash or Greninja's Ice Beam for Honchkrow.

You can't escape this one, and both sides' Defence is boosted on entry, his more. Honchkrow (Night Slash, Drill Peck, Steel Wing, Tailwind), Mega Heracross (Skill Link: Pin Missile, Brick Break, Rock Blast, Bulldoze), Alolan Muk (Gunk Shot, Crunch, Ice Punch, Minimize), Rocky Helmet Ferrothorn (Iron Barbs: Power Whip, Gyro Ball, Thunder Wave, Ingrain).

items.html: Arcanine's Flamethrower is 4x on Ferrothorn (special, so Iron Barbs and Rocky Helmet don't punish it) and 2x on Mega Heracross.
Gardevoir's Psychic is 2x on Mega Heracross. Mamoswine's Earthquake is 2x on Alolan Muk; kill Muk before Minimize stacks.
Mamoswine's Icicle Crash is 2x on Honchkrow, and Greninja's Specs Ice Beam OHKOs it (173 to 205%, Difficult set).
Keep your Heracross away from Honchkrow (Drill Peck is 4x) and your Absol away from Mega Heracross (Brick Break and Pin Missile are 2x).
Reward: Heracronite, which is your Heracross's Mega Stone. From here it can Mega Evolve (Skill Link: Pin Missile and Rock Blast always hit five times).

blocks.html: Heavier Pokémon move first here. Lead Mega Metagross. Greninja's Specs Grass Knot kills Mudsdale and Wailord (bring Greninja in after a KO). Heracross's Brick Break for Pangoro and Snorlax, Aerial Ace for Hariyama. Never burn or poison Hariyama (Guts).

Part 1, the Ring Challenge: three 1v1s against Sawk, Poliwrath and Emboar (Lv 50) with one mon. You're healed between rounds but can't swap. Flying, Psychic and Fairy moves are disabled. Use Mega Metagross: Bulldoze (TM96, Blizzard Mart; 2x on Emboar), Thunder Punch (2x on Poliwrath; free tutor in Dehara), Iron Head and Hammer Arm. Earthquake isn't available until after this gym. None of those types is disabled.

Part 2, Big Mo. Permanent weight-based Trick Room: heavier mons move first (TV Tropes; the Reddit guide you found mentions the weight rule too). Three of his mons carry Heavy Slam, which hits harder the lighter the target is, and it's Steel, so it's 2x on Fairies. nuzlockeredux lists five mons; on Difficult he also had Mega Lucario, so be ready for a sixth.

blocks.html: Prep: bag 2 Hyper Potions, 1 Revive, 1 Full Heal. Don't bring Will-O-Wisp or Toxic for Hariyama (Guts).

items.html: Lead Mega Metagross. It resists Heavy Slam, Body Slam, Rock Slide and Smack Down. Earthquake, High Horsepower, Wicked Blow, Knock Off and Crunch are 2x on it.

Mudsdale: Greninja's Specs Grass Knot OHKOs it (Grass Knot is 120 power against anything this heavy, and Stamina only raises Defence). Greninja is light, so Mudsdale moves first: its Earthquake does 83 to 98% to Greninja before Protean has changed its type, so bring Greninja in after a KO, not on an attack. Backup: Mamoswine's Icicle Crash (68 to 81%) twice. Never Gardevoir in front of it: Heavy Slam OHKOs.

Pangoro: Heracross. Wicked Blow (always a crit) does only 51 to 60%, Drain Punch is resisted, and Brick Break OHKOs it. Get Metagross out: Wicked Blow has a 69% chance to OHKO it. Gardevoir's Dazzling Gleam is the other answer.
Snorlax: Heracross's Brick Break (73 to 87%) or Arcanine's Close Combat (55 to 64%). Thick Fat halves Fire and Ice. Its Body Slam does 43 to 52% to Heracross.
Hariyama: Heracross's Aerial Ace (63 to 75%) or Mega Metagross's Psychic (55 to 65%). Guts: never burn or poison it.
Wailord: Greninja's Specs Grass Knot (OHKO). Its Ice Beam only does 20 to 24% to Greninja. Regenerator heals it on switch-out, so finish it; Clear Smog wipes your boosts.

blocks.html: Expect the switch: under the weight rule, most of his mons are heavier than yours, so they move first and never dodge. The exceptions are Mega Metagross (the heaviest thing in the fight) and Mamoswine (heavier than Pangoro and Hariyama), so those two are the only attackers he might switch away from. I can't tell whether Unbound's AI understands the weight rule when it decides who moves first, so treat that part as a guess. Wailord is the sure one: Regenerator mons switch out to heal once they're under half HP and facing a hit that would KO them. Hit it with Grass Knot from full HP and it never gets the chance.

blocks.title: Great Desert, Gurun Town and Seaport City (cap 57)

blocks.html: What you'll do: Rock Climb opens the Great Desert. Get Earthquake, pass through Gurun Town, and reach Seaport City: a big shopping stop with the Super Rod, the bazaar and the Battle Frontier. Two warehouse fights finish it.
Joining your team: Togekiss (Togetic plus a Shiny Stone) if it isn't evolved yet; Rotom from Mission #077 for Gym 7.
Bosses: Swizer & Bullo (West Warehouse, Ice and Fairy types only), then the Science Society scientist (East Warehouse).

items.html: Get Rock Climb. Sources disagree on where HM08 comes from: an NPC on Route 16 or on Route 17. The Rock Climb return trip box below lists what it opens up, including TM79 Dark Pulse for Houndoom.
Walk Routes 15 to 17 into the Great Desert and grab TM26 Earthquake first: it's directly above the Tomb of Borrius (needs Rock Smash and Rock Climb). Teach it to Garchomp.
Pass through Gurun Town to Seaport City.
In Seaport, get the Super Rod from the Fisherman at the Port (another return trip box).
Shop: TM53 Energy Ball is 20,000 at the bazaar (for Gardevoir). The Battle Frontier opens on NG+ with your carried Frontier Card: spend BP on Gold Bottle Caps (200 BP) for new team members.
Start Mission #077 (Too Much TV): find five TV-afflicted kids around Borrius and you get a Rotom, which you want for Gym 7.
Evolve Togetic into Togekiss with a Shiny Stone if you haven't already. The next fight needs it.
West Warehouse: Swizer & Bullo. Your team has to be Ice or Fairy types only (dual types count). Four goon doubles come first.
East Warehouse: the Science Society scientist. A wild Electivire, then a Dynamax Electivire double, then the scientist. You get an Elekid egg, the Electirizer, a Power Weight and a Gold Bottle Cap.

blocks.html: Why it's hard: four Electric types, so your Water and Flying mons are liabilities; two of them Levitate past Ground moves, Manectric's Flame Orb powers up its Flamethrower, and Magnezone has Sturdy plus a Weakness Policy.
Bring: Mamoswine, Garchomp, Arcanine, Absol, Mega Metagross, Gardevoir. Leave Greninja and Azumarill home (Electric is 2x on Water) and Heracross too (Vikavolt's Air Slash is 4x on it).

items.html: Lead Mamoswine. Immune to Electric, and the Scarf Earthquake OHKOs Manectric. Ground misses Rotom-Mow and Vikavolt (Levitate) and Magnezone once it uses Magnet Rise.
Rotom-Mow: switch to Absol and Megahorn (OHKO). Rotom is faster and its Thunderbolt does 75 to 89%, so Absol takes one hit and kills. Shadow Ball is resisted.
Vikavolt: Arcanine's Flare Blitz (OHKO; Fire Gem tutor or Lv 60) or Flamethrower (89 to 107%). Its Thunderbolt does 58 to 69% to Arcanine.

Magnezone: don't hit it super effectively from full. Sturdy keeps it at 1 HP and the Weakness Policy gives it +2 to both attacking stats. Chip it first with a neutral hit (Metagross's Zen Headbutt, or anything that doesn't kill), then finish with Arcanine's Fire or Garchomp's Earthquake (4x, if it hasn't used Magnet Rise). Its Hidden Power Ice has an 88% chance to OHKO Garchomp, so Garchomp only comes in to finish.

blocks.html: Expect the switch: Manectric is slower than Scarf Mamoswine, and Rotom-Mow and Vikavolt are both immune to Earthquake, but neither qualifies as a switch-in: they're slower than Mamoswine and Icicle Crash hits them too hard to count as a wall. So Manectric stays in and eats the Earthquake. Rotom-Mow is faster than Absol, so it never dodges Megahorn. Nothing here has Lightning Rod or Volt Absorb.

blocks.html: Prep: bag 2 Hyper Potions, 1 Full Heal (Toxic Spikes), 1 Max Revive. Reorder every team member's moves before you talk to her.
Turn by turn

items.html: Kill Mega Gyarados first. Unbound Wiki's top tip. Mold Breaker plus Dragon Dance plus Earthquake runs through everything. Azumarill's Play Rough or Gardevoir's Moonblast (2x) the moment it appears.

Toxapex is passive: Toxic Spikes, Haze, Recover, Regenerator. Don't set up while it's alive (Haze). Garchomp's Earthquake (2x: Ground hits Poison). The Reddit guide you found links a write-up of beating Expert Tessy's Toxapex with your own status moves instead of brute force: a Taunt user stops Recover and Haze, and Clefable's Magic Guard ignores Toxic.
Kingdra: Moonblast or Play Rough (2x). Its Ice Beam is 4x on Garchomp and 2x on Togekiss.

Seismitoad: Ludicolo's Giga Drain (4x), or Greninja's Specs Grass Knot (4x on its Water/Ground typing: 200 to 237%, OHKO). Order Greninja's moves Grass Knot, Surf so it starts Grass/Water, which takes a quarter from her Water moves. Seismitoad is faster in the rain and its Earthquake does 45 to 52%, so Greninja takes one hit; keep it away from Armaldo, whose X-Scissor OHKOs it once Protean has made it Grass.
Armaldo: Togekiss's Air Slash or Rotom's Thunderbolt (2x each).
Seaking: its Poison Jab and Smart Strike hit Fairies 2x. Garchomp's Earthquake (2x) or Rotom's Thunderbolt (2x).
Azumarill can Belly Drum once Toxapex is gone; +6 Play Rough or Aqua Jet KOs anything she has.

blocks.html: Sticky Web helps here. The community guide suggests slowing her Swift Swimmers with Sticky Web (Araquanid, Charjabug, or Ribombee). Under Sticky Web plus rain, Ludicolo outspeeds them.

Expect the switch: in the rain, Swift Swim doubles the Speed of four of hers, so they attack instead of dodging. Mega Gyarados has no Swift Swim, but nothing on her team walls Azumarill or Gardevoir, so it stays in too. Toxapex is the switcher: with Regenerator, once it's under half HP and facing a hit that would KO it, it switches out to heal a third. Either take it from full in one go, or when it's low, click the move that's good on her likely switch-in rather than on Toxapex.

items.html: His Mamoswine leads with a Sash and Stealth Rock. Mega Evolve Heracross and Arm Thrust: five hits break the Sash and kill (108 to 134%). His Mamoswine is faster than Heracross, so it gets one hit in first; that's also why the AI won't switch it out (it only dodges when it's slower).

Chandelure: Greninja's Dark Pulse (OHKO; Greninja is faster). Shadow Tag means you can't switch out once it's in, so make sure the mon in front of it can kill it. Its Energy Ball OHKOs Greninja, so this only works because Greninja moves first.
Aggron: Mega Heracross's Arm Thrust (OHKO through Sturdy). Its Shuca Berry only stops Ground.
Rotom-Fan: Mamoswine's Icicle Crash (OHKO). Motor Drive absorbs Electric, so no Electric moves.
Vaporeon: Greninja's Grass Knot (2HKO) or Gardevoir's Energy Ball. Never Surf into it (Water Absorb).
Mega Garchomp comes last: Greninja's Specs Ice Beam (OHKO, Greninja is faster). Its Dragon Rush OHKOs Greninja back if you miss, so keep Togekiss ready to switch in.

items.html: Heracross into Aggron: Fighting can't touch Chandelure, so if Chandelure is still alive the AI may switch it in to take Arm Thrust. Then Shadow Tag traps Heracross and Flamethrower is 2x on it. Kill Chandelure before you go for Aggron, or use Rock Blast (2x on Chandelure) if you see it coming.
Greninja's Surf is an open invitation for Vaporeon (Water Absorb). Don't click Surf while Vaporeon is alive.

Mega Garchomp facing Ice Beam, or Rotom-Fan facing Icicle Crash: Vaporeon, Aggron and his Mamoswine all resist Ice, but the AI only dodges into a mon that walls your attacker, and each of those takes a 2HKO from one of its other moves (Grass Knot on Vaporeon, Surf on Aggron and Mamoswine; Earthquake from your Mamoswine on Aggron and his Mamoswine). So by the engine rules they shouldn't come in. If Unbound's AI does it anyway, hit the switch-in with that move next turn.

blocks.html: Greninja's Specs Ice Beam kills Zekrom on turn 1 (Greninja is faster). Then swap Greninja out. Fairy moves hit both 2x, and your Fairies are immune to their Dragon moves. Leave Absol out.

Lv 62. TV Tropes says boss legendaries get Totem-style stat boosts. Zekrom: Fusion Bolt, Dragon Claw, Crunch, Zen Headbutt. Reshiram: Fusion Flare, Dragon Pulse, Ancient Power, Extrasensory. v2.1 changed the Expert pair to a Sp. Atk (Reshiram) or Attack (Zekrom) boost only, with max EVs.

items.html: Greninja kills Zekrom on turn 1. It's faster, and Specs Ice Beam OHKOs Zekrom (107 to 127%). Do that first: a +1 Fusion Bolt does more than double Greninja's HP. Ice is only neutral on Reshiram (46 to 54%), and a boosted Dragon Pulse is about a coin flip to OHKO Greninja, so swap it out after Zekrom drops.

Fairy and Ice hit both 2x. Specs Gardevoir's Dazzling Gleam has a 50% chance to OHKO Zekrom (92 to 109%, before its boost) and hits both. Both Fairies are immune to their Dragon moves. (Gardevoir and Greninja can't both hold the Specs; give it to whichever leads.)
Leave Absol out: a boosted Fusion Flare or Dragon Claw OHKOs it.
Zekrom's Zen Headbutt does 36 to 43% to Togekiss.
Unbound Wiki's tip: Alolan Ninetales with Icium Z can delete Zekrom on turn 1.

blocks.html: Absol's Sucker Punch kills Mega Alakazam (if it Nasty Plots instead of attacking, Knock Off that turn). Greninja's Dark Pulse for Mismagius, Ice Beam for Mandibuzz. items.html: Mega Alakazam is the threat. It's faster than everything you have, its Energy Ball OHKOs Greninja, and Nasty Plot snowballs. Answer: Absol's Sucker Punch (OHKO). Absol takes 69 to 81% from Energy Ball if Alakazam targets it first, but Sucker Punch moves first anyway. The one risk: if Alakazam uses Nasty Plot instead of attacking, Sucker Punch fails; Knock Off it that turn instead.
Mismagius: Greninja's Specs Dark Pulse (OHKO, Greninja is faster). Its Thunderbolt does 78 to 93% to Greninja. Absol's Knock Off OHKOs it too, but Dazzling Gleam does 83 to 98% to Absol.

Toxicroak: Focus Sash. Mega Garchomp's Earthquake twice (the first one leaves it at 1 HP), or Gardevoir's Psychic (4x) plus any finisher. Its Ice Punch does 83 to 100% to Garchomp, so keep Garchomp healthy for this one.

Incineroar: physical hits only (Assault Vest). Garchomp's Earthquake (88 to 104% before Intimidate) or Azumarill's Banded Aqua Tail. Intimidate drops your physical attackers on entry; Greninja's Surf ignores that but only does 48 to 58% through the Vest.
Mandibuzz: Rocky Helmet punishes contact and Foul Play uses your own Attack. Greninja's Ice Beam (89 to 106%) is the clean answer.
Eelektross: Levitate, no real weakness. Garchomp walls it (Flamethrower 15 to 18%) and Dragon Claws it down, or Greninja's Surf twice.
Sandstorm chips Absol, Greninja, Gardevoir and Azumarill every turn. Garchomp and Metagross are immune.

blocks.html: Expect the switch:

items.html: Gardevoir's Psychic on Toxicroak invites Incineroar. Incineroar is immune to Psychic, and with its Assault Vest nothing Gardevoir has even 3HKOs it (Moonblast does 27 to 33%), so if Gardevoir is faster than Toxicroak the AI has a perfect switch. Use Garchomp's Earthquake (the main plan) or Metagross's Zen Headbutt instead: Metagross is slower than Toxicroak, so Toxicroak attacks rather than dodging, and Incineroar takes 2x from Metagross's Earthquake, so it isn't a wall against Metagross anyway.

Garchomp's Earthquake on Incineroar: Mismagius and Eelektross are immune (Levitate). Eelektross is too slow and too frail physically to count, but Mismagius can come in if it's faster than your Garchomp. Killing Mismagius early (step 2) removes that.

Absol's Sucker Punch on Mega Alakazam: priority means Absol moves first, so Alakazam could dodge, but nothing on his team walls Absol (Play Rough hits Incineroar, Mandibuzz and Toxicroak at least neutral), so it stays in. Sucker Punch fails if Alakazam uses Nasty Plot instead of attacking, so expect to miss once.
Mandibuzz's Rocky Helmet: the AI can bring it in on a contact move that would leave you KO'd by the Helmet. Don't Sucker Punch or Knock Off when Absol is under about a sixth of its HP.

blocks.html: Greninja's Specs Ice Beam kills each Mega Rayquaza (Hoopa summons a second one). Absol's Play Rough kills Hoopa; hit first or come in after a KO, because its Drain Punch nearly kills Absol. Fairy moves hit both 2x.
Lv 62. Hoopa summons another Rayquaza after the first goes down. Delta Stream removes Rayquaza's Flying weaknesses, so Ice is only 2x on it.

items.html: Greninja deletes Mega Rayquaza: Specs Ice Beam OHKOs it (208 to 246%) even with Delta Stream, which only removes its Flying weaknesses. Rayquaza's Extreme Speed (priority) does 47 to 56% to Greninja, so Greninja gets its shot. Hoopa brings a second Rayquaza after the first falls; Ice Beam it again.

Absol handles Hoopa Unbound: immune to Zen Headbutt, Hyperspace Fury does 45 to 53%, and Life Orb Play Rough OHKOs Hoopa (135 to 160%). Its Drain Punch (91 to 108%) is the one to fear, so hit first or come in after a KO.
Fairy hits both 2x: Togekiss, Gardevoir and Azumarill do the work.
Rayquaza's Extreme Speed outprioritises Ice Shard, so don't count on outspeeding it.
Afterwards, use the Prison Bottle: Hoopa Confined (Lv 60) joins you.

blocks.html: Absol and Heracross stay home. Lead Mega Metagross + Houndoom (Houndoom holds the Safety Goggles). Meteor Mash kills Mega Gardevoir first, then Comfey and Primarina. Houndoom's Flamethrower for Roserade; Flash Fire eats Mega Gardevoir's Mystical Fire. Ice Shard then Icicle Crash for Dragonite.

Why it's hard: five of six hit with Fairy or Fire, Roserade has a Wide Lens Sleep Powder, Togedemaru's Fake Out and Nuzzle waste your turns, and Dragonite's Multiscale halves your first hit. The sandstorm chips anything that isn't Rock, Ground or Steel.

blocks.html: If you only bring three: Mega Metagross, Houndoom and Mamoswine (Greninja if you'd rather have speed over Mamoswine's bulk). Absol and Heracross stay home: Fairy is 2x on both.

items.html: Lead Mega Metagross + Houndoom. Togedemaru will Fake Out or Nuzzle. Houndoom's Goggles stop Roserade's Sleep Powder.
Mega Gardevoir first: Meteor Mash (OHKO). Its Mystical Fire is 2x on Metagross (62 to 73%), so if it targets Houndoom instead, Flash Fire absorbs it and powers up Houndoom's Fire moves.
Roserade: Houndoom's Flamethrower (OHKO) or Greninja's Ice Beam (OHKO).
Togedemaru: Sturdy and an Air Balloon (so Earthquake misses). Flamethrower takes it to 1 HP, then anything finishes. Don't waste a big hit on it early.
Dragonite: Mamoswine's Ice Shard, then Icicle Crash. Or bring Greninja in after a KO and Ice Beam it (OHKO even through Multiscale).
Comfey and Primarina: Meteor Mash. Comfey's Babiri Berry halves the first Steel hit. Primarina's Hyper Voice turns into a Water move (Liquid Voice), which is 2x on Houndoom and Mamoswine.

blocks.html: Expect the switch: this is a double battle, and the engine's dodge-a-KO switch only exists in singles, so the AI shouldn't pull a mon out just because you can OHKO it. It still switches in a mon that absorbs your attack, and none of hers absorbs Fire, Steel, Ice or Dark. If one of hers ends up with only useless moves (Togedemaru's Electric moves into Garchomp and Mamoswine, say), it may swap that one out.

Why it's hard: Sableye's Prankster Will-O-Wisp and Quash, Krookodile's Intimidate, a Mega Beedrill with Adaptability that outspeeds and OHKOs most things, Swoobat's Helping Hand and Sash, and sandstorm chip. Your rival is your partner, so you control one side.

lead_fields: Your rival partners you, so the game has you pick three (see the Cootes rival section). The first three are the plan; the other three are swaps.

blocks.html: Your three: Arcanine, Greninja and Absol. Gardevoir is the swap if you want an answer to Tentacruel that doesn't rely on your rival.

items.html: Lead Arcanine + Greninja. Intimidate cuts Krookodile, Dusknoir and Mega Beedrill. Sableye's Will-O-Wisp can't burn Arcanine and doesn't matter to Greninja (special).
Mega Beedrill first: Arcanine's Flare Blitz (OHKO). It's faster than everything you have, and its Adaptability Poison Jab nearly OHKOs Greninja (95 to 112%), so this is the priority.
Krookodile: Greninja's Grass Knot (OHKO). Don't Surf it: the Passho Berry halves the first Water hit.
Dusknoir: Greninja's Dark Pulse (85 to 101%) or Absol's Knock Off twice.
Swoobat: Knock Off or Dark Pulse takes it to 1 HP through the Sash; a second hit or Extreme Speed finishes it. Unaware means your boosts don't matter to it.
Sableye: Absol's Play Rough (2HKO). Its Prankster moves fail on Absol.
Tentacruel: Gardevoir's Psychic (2x). It Hazes boosts, so don't bother setting up while it's alive.

blocks.html: Expect the switch: double battle, so no dodge-a-KO switching under the engine rules. The only absorb risk is minor: nothing on his side absorbs Fire, Grass, Dark or Fairy.

Turn by turn

items.html: Lead Mamoswine and get Stealth Rock up. Every devolved form takes rock damage again when it comes back in.
Forretress sets screens and has Counter. Metagross's Brick Break removes them; then Arcanine's Flamethrower (4x; special, so Counter does nothing).
Araquanid: Mirror Coat only reflects special hits, so use physical (Garchomp's Stone Edge, Metagross's Meteor Mash). Water Bubble halves Fire, so keep Arcanine off it.
Volcarona: hit it with Rock or Water before Quiver Dance: Garchomp's Stone Edge (OHKO). Its Heat Wave OHKOs Mamoswine, so switch Mamoswine out the moment it appears.
Burn Flygon and Drapion with Arcanine's Will-O-Wisp. Then Mamoswine's Icicle Crash (Flygon) and Garchomp's Earthquake (Drapion).
Mega Scizor: Arcanine's Flamethrower (72 to 85%). He Max Potions it below half, so finish it in two quick hits.
Count devolutions. Each evolved mon of his has to be beaten two or three times. Pace your healing items.

blocks.html: Expect the switch (single battle, so the AI dodges KOs when it's slower than you):

items.html: Arcanine's Flamethrower on Forretress (4x, and Arcanine is much faster): expect Araquanid to come in. Water Bubble plus its Water typing cuts Fire to a quarter. Have Garchomp or Metagross ready to come in on it, and use physical moves (Mirror Coat only reflects special).

Garchomp's Stone Edge on Volcarona (Garchomp is just faster): Flygon resists Rock, but Garchomp's Scale Shot is 2x on it, so Flygon doesn't count as a wall and shouldn't switch in. If it does anyway, Scale Shot: four hits from a Life Orb Garchomp OHKO it (171 to 202%).
Greninja's Surf on Volcarona: Araquanid resists Water and can come in, then Mirror Coat Greninja's next special hit. If Araquanid appears, switch Greninja out rather than attacking it.

Once his mons are devolved and slow (Larvesta, Vibrava, Trapinch), they're usually slower than you, so expect them to switch out to dodge too. Stealth Rock punishes every one of those switches, which is why Mamoswine leads with it.
